[Śāstra] There are sixty-five cases of receiving full ordination when one has not yet reached the required age.

[Commentary]: Generally, those who have reached the age of twenty possess fully developed resolve and character, their aspirations are far-reaching, they can endure external conditions and afflictions, and their minds are settled within the restraints of the precepts.
Thus, they are capable of cultivating the Path, advancing through the stages, and attaining ultimate success; it is therefore appropriate that they receive ordination so that the Dharma may flourish.

Those of younger years whose age is not yet full possess immature and weak dispositions; they cannot yet endure various sufferings and are prone to violating the precepts. Since there is no means for them to advance on the Path, [they should not be ordained].
This was established because [the offense] contravenes the holy teachings and causes irreparable damage.
Regarding the first section of the sixty-fifth rule, it is divided into two parts. First, the benefits of reaching the required age are set forth in three points:

(1) establishing one’s resolve and aspiring toward the distant goal; (2) enduring hardships while guarding the precepts; and (3) advancing on the path to achieve success. "Endurance" (*kṣānti*) means to remain calm and composed.

The dwelling [of the precepts] is briefly explained below in two parts: first, the loss incurred by failing to fulfill them; second, the benefits resulting from fulfilling them, as can be seen from the corresponding text.

[Commentary: However, the obstacles and prohibitions are not limited to one; none are permitted or accepted. Yet, among these, the single category of "obstacles" (*antarāyika-dharma*) carries the meaning that one cannot obtain the precepts.

As for the remaining various obstacles, their essential types are not uniform, such as those like blue or white [colors], or fixed difficulties that cannot be changed, or [the requirements for] robes and bowls, and so forth.

**[Vinaya]** One who has reached twenty years of age should receive the full precepts (*upasampadā*).

**[Commentary]** The Buddha said: "If one has not reached twenty years of age, they are unable to endure cold and heat, hunger and thirst, wind and rain, mosquitoes, gadflies, venomous insects, or harsh words; nor can they endure physical pain, nor can they maintain the precepts."
